title: nccw-utm-1998-southern-heritage
label: The Crippler
how: Won the vacant title by pinfall over Essex with a DDT; lost it by submission to Bobby "Bad Apple" Durango.

title: nccw-utm-1998-southern-heritage
label: Bobby "Bad Apple" Durango
note: Still holding the title as of the last card this record holds (3 March 1998), where he also won the Television Championship in the same match, becoming the promotion's first double champion.

title: nccw-utm-1998-television
label: "Cajun" Huey Armstrong
how: Won the newly created title by pinfall over the Crippler; lost it by pinfall to Bobby "Bad Apple" Durango in a winner-take-all match that also carried the Southern Heritage belt.

title: nccw-utm-1998-television
label: Bobby "Bad Apple" Durango
note: Still champion as of the last card this record holds. A fellow Usenet participant's own signature line, dated six weeks later, credits a different wrestler as the reigning, undefeated Television Champion at the promotion's own fold -- an unresolved discrepancy with no card of its own surviving to settle it.

title: nccw-utm-1998-world-heavyweight
label: "The Natural Wonder" Max Maxwell

lost.source: No card documenting a title change survives; bounded only by the last held card (3 March 1998) and outside corroboration naming a new champion (4 April 1998).

how: Won the vacant title in a tournament final by submission over the Mad Goat; successfully defended it by submission over "Lucky" Lambert on 3 March 1998, the last card this record holds.
note: A fellow Usenet participant's own signature line on an unrelated newsgroup post, dated 4 April 1998, credits Bobby "Bad Apple" Durango as NCCW World Champion instead; no NCCW-authored document of the title change survives, and how or when Maxwell lost it is unrecorded.

title: nccw-utm-1998-world-heavyweight
label: Bobby "Bad Apple" Durango

won.source: A fellow Usenet participant's own signature line on an unrelated newsgroup post, dated 4 April 1998, names him "NCCW World Champion"; no NCCW-authored document of the title change survives.

note: The promotion is described as "now-closed" ten days later, 14 April 1998, in a scattered members' own thread; no further title activity survives.
